title: Computer Programming I
description: The CCMAS first programming course, taught in Java: programming languages and their generations, programming paradigms and approaches, pseudocode and flowcharts, data types, variables and strings, operators and selection, loops, and arrays and methods. Built from Dr B. I. Ayinla's COS 201 lecture notes (Weeks 1 to 6) and the arrays, modularity and methods slides.

topics.title: Programming Languages and Their Generations
topics.summary: A programming language is a formal set of rules and syntax for writing instructions a computer can execute. Languages are classified into five generations, from machine language to natural and AI-based languages, and are translated by compilers or interpreters; Java compiles to bytecode run by the JVM.
subtopics: Structure of a first Java program

topics.title: Programming Paradigms
topics.summary: A paradigm is the style of constructs a program uses. Functional programming evaluates pure functions and avoids mutable state; declarative programming states what to compute rather than how; logic programming uses facts, rules and queries, as in Prolog; and scripting languages are interpreted, dynamically typed languages for automation.
subtopics: Functional programming: pure functions and immutability
Lambda expressions and recursion in Java
Declarative programming: SQL, HTML and Java Streams
Logic programming: facts, rules, queries and Prolog

topics.title: Programming Approaches, Pseudocode and Flowcharts
topics.summary: A programming approach is the strategy used to design and structure a solution: top-down, bottom-up, structured, modular or object-oriented. Good programmers design first with pseudocode and flowcharts, then translate the design into Java.

topics.title: Data Types, Variables and Strings
topics.summary: Java is strongly typed: every variable has a declared type. It has eight primitive types plus reference types such as String and arrays. Variables are named memory locations, constants are declared final, type casting can be widening or narrowing, and Strings are immutable objects with many built-in methods.
subtopics: Strings, string methods and Scanner input

topics.title: Operators and Selection Statements
topics.summary: Operators build expressions: arithmetic, assignment, relational and logical operators, evaluated by precedence. Selection lets a program choose a path with if, if-else, the else-if ladder, nested if, switch and the ternary operator.
subtopics: Operator precedence and the ternary operator
if, if-else and the else-if ladder
Nested if and the switch statement

topics.title: Loops and Iteration
topics.summary: Iteration repeats a block of code a fixed number of times or while a condition holds. Java has for, while, do-while and enhanced for-each loops, with break and continue to control them, and nested loops for tables and patterns.
subtopics: break, continue and the enhanced for loop

topics.title: Arrays and Methods
topics.summary: An array is a fixed-size, zero-indexed collection of elements of the same type, traversed with loops, extended to 2D arrays and supported by java.util.Arrays. Methods group statements under a name for modularity and reuse, with parameters, return values, overloading and recursion.
subtopics: Arrays: fixed size, zero-indexed, same type
